objective: Judge 24 batch-2 registry directions (ETF-level, per the owner's 2026-09-28 assignment) into lane-testable candidates, stock-level handoffs, or documented not-executable/evidence-too-weak verdicts.

sources.credibility: author (David P. Simon, Bentley University) published on SSRN, later in Journal of Derivatives & Hedge Funds (2011); studies BEP's own NAV premium anomaly, not a trading rule
sources.core_claim: S&P 500 Covered Call Fund Inc. (BEP) traded at premiums to NAV up to 23% in 2007 despite a transparent, easy-to-replicate one-month at-the-money SPX covered-call strategy; the premium is linked to return-overreaction and a VIX spike.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds dir:covered_call_cef_income_pwb; BEP itself liquidated 2010-02-02 (SEC EDGAR N-CSR), so this round substitutes XYLD as an honest, cited buy-and-hold proxy for the same monthly covered-call mechanism.
sources.reflection: Overfit risk low (it is a documented historical anomaly, not a fitted rule); decay risk is moot since the exact fund is gone; cost sensitivity untested here since XYLD_COVERED_CALL_PROXY is buy-and-hold with no signal-driven turnover beyond drift.

sources.credibility: paperswithbacktest replication of Caporin, de Roon & Pelizzon (2009); page does not disclose the exact mean-reversion formula, only a 1990-2026 replication summary
sources.core_claim: A mean-variance-optimal, mean-reversion-exploiting tactical allocation across 16 positions (mostly individual stocks plus a bond index, not a pure ETF universe) reports 9.82% CAGR / Sharpe 1.22 / -25.98% max drawdown in the paperswithbacktest re-run.
sources.project_applicability: 16-position universe is mixed individual-stock/index, not ETF-level, and the exact signal formula is not published on the page -- handed to the stock-level agent rather than tested in this ETF-only batch.
sources.reflection: Cannot assess overfit/decay without the exact rule; paperswithbacktest's own replication methodology re-fits parameters to 1990-2026, a known source of look-ahead risk this batch does not resolve.

sources.credibility: paperswithbacktest replication of Santos & Torrent (2022); 208-position universe confirmed to be individual S&P 500 constituents
sources.core_claim: Combining mean-variance optimization with four trend-following signals across 208 S&P 500 stocks, daily rebalance, reports 19.87% CAGR / Sharpe 1.09 / -51.32% max drawdown.
sources.project_applicability: Stock-level (208 individual names), handed to the stock-level agent; the -51% drawdown at only 1.09 Sharpe is a weak risk-adjusted shape regardless.
sources.reflection: Daily rebalance across 208 names implies high turnover/cost sensitivity not evaluated on the page; decay risk unassessed since replication window includes 2026 (post-hoc).

sources.credibility: paperswithbacktest replication of Todorov (2021); page does not disclose which of leverage/calendar/flow rebalancing effect drives the replicated rule
sources.core_claim: ETF rebalancing (leverage, calendar, or flow-driven) measurably distorts VIX and commodity ETF prices; paperswithbacktest's own replication reports only 2.79% CAGR at Sharpe 1.00.
sources.project_applicability: Exact replicable rule undisclosed and the mechanism may need flow/creation-redemption data we do not have; marked not_executable pending the primary paper.
sources.reflection: Low absolute return (2.79%/yr) even in the source's own replication suggests limited near-term profit potential even if the exact rule were obtained.

sources.credibility: paperswithbacktest replication of Etheber (2014); 26-position universe confirmed to be individual stocks
sources.core_claim: Simple moving-average trading rules generate abnormal trading volume (25-55% higher on buy signals, 15-25% on sell signals) around signal days; paperswithbacktest's own replication reports 11.27% CAGR / Sharpe 1.01 / -34.92% drawdown.
sources.project_applicability: Stock-level (26 individual names), handed to the stock-level agent; thematically adjacent to the already-refuted local giants_sweep_20260922 (0/24 published SMA/trend ETF rules) and lightgbm_price_volume_recipe_v1 findings that price-volume features on this kind of universe are exhausted.
sources.reflection: Barely clears a 1.0 Sharpe bar with a 35% drawdown even in the source's favorable replication; low expected marginal value.

sources.credibility: secondary blog summarizing Graziani (2024, SSRN, 'Time Series Reversal: An End-of-the-Month Perspective') and a 2022 NTNU thesis; primary SSRN paper not independently opened this pass
sources.core_claim: S&P 500 end-of-month returns (4th Friday to month-end) are negatively correlated with the following month's return, both in-sample and out-of-sample, over a 45-year period; does not require shorting.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds EOM_REVERSAL_SPY's exact rule (long next month iff this month's 4th-Friday-to-month-end return was negative); no quantified CAGR/Sharpe/drawdown given in the secondary source, so this round supplies its own via scripts/screen_batch.py.
sources.reflection: Secondary source risk: no independent verification of Graziani's own numbers in this pass; decay risk unassessed beyond the source's own out-of-sample claim.

sources.credibility: practitioner replication built on a peer-reviewed citation chain (Lucca & Moench 2015 JoF; Savor & Wilson 2013 JFQA; Cieslak, Morse & Vissing-Jorgensen 2019 JoF; Liu, Tang & Zhou 2022 JFE); own backtest, not third-party verified
sources.core_claim: Pre-FOMC announcement drift (long from the close before a scheduled FOMC meeting through the close of its final day) remains persistent through Dec 2024; leveraged-ETF variant delivers after-cost CAGR 8-9%, Sharpe ~0.6, trading only 5% of days.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds FOMC_DRIFT_SPY and FOMC_DRIFT_TQQQ's exact entry/exit rule; this round's own FOMC meeting dates come from federalreserve.gov, not from this blog.
sources.reflection: Sharpe ~0.6 in the source's own SPY-level numbers is below the K1 bar (80% of S3's 1.49/0.81) on priors alone; a clean refutation is the likely, still-useful outcome.

sources.credibility: practitioner replication (Hull Tactical), cross-checked against etftrends.com's independent S&P 500 futures replication and a 2022 NTNU academic thesis summarized by harbourfrontquant.substack.com
sources.core_claim: Turn-of-month (buy SPY close of last trading day of month, sell close of 4th trading day of next month) captures 44% of total return (before dividends) while invested ~20% of trading days.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds TOM_SPY's exact hold window (4th trading day, not 3rd or 5th).
sources.reflection: Before-dividends-only number likely overstates net edge; this round's own 10/20bp cost view will show whether the edge survives realistic costs.

sources.credibility: primary official source, the U.S. central bank's own published meeting calendar
sources.core_claim: The FOMC holds eight regularly scheduled meetings per year; exact 2021-2027 dates are published, with historical archive pages for 2015-2020.
sources.project_applicability: Directly used as the hard-coded FOMC_MEETINGS date list in scripts/screen_batches/h20260928_05_batch2.py -- exactly what the brief requires (dates copied from the Fed's calendar, never inferred from price).
sources.reflection: No overfit/decay risk: this is a public calendar fact, not a fitted parameter.

sources.credibility: primary official source, the fund's own SEC-filed N-CSR annual report
sources.core_claim: S&P 500 Covered Call Fund Inc. (BEP) liquidated on 2010-01-29 and distributed all proceeds on 2010-02-02.
sources.project_applicability: Confirms BEP is not tradable today, justifying the XYLD_COVERED_CALL_PROXY substitution (an honest, cited, currently-tradable proxy) rather than silently building a candidate around a dead ticker.
sources.reflection: No overfit/decay risk: this is a historical corporate-action fact, not a fitted parameter.
